failed().notice: Returns true if any test assertion has failed.

targetSenders().notice: Returns sender allowlist configured via `targetSender` (empty means no sender allowlist).

test_CancelBeforeExpiry().notice: cancel() still works on a non-expired pending proposal.

test_FullLifecycle_ProposeVoteExecute().notice: End-to-end lifecycle test: one approver proposes, two distinct approvers vote (reaching quorum), then anyone executes with the original payload. Verifies that: (1) the Proposed event is emitted, (2) two Voted events emitted, (3) approvalCount reaches quorum, (4) USDC moves on execute, (5) executed flag is set.

test_GovernanceCannotProduceUnreachableQ.notice: Governance change cannot produce an unreachable quorum state via the duplicate-approver path. A CONFIG_CHANGE with [addrA, addrA] and quorum=2 passes the propose-time check (raw length=2) but reverts at execute time because _setApprovers deduplicates to 1 unique address and then checks quorum=2 > 1. This test links to test_RevertIf_ConfigDuplicateApproversBreaksQuorum and serves as an explicit requirement anchor. REQUIREMENT: the contract MUST prevent governance from producing a state where quorum > deduplicated approver count, regardless of how the proposal was crafted.

test_GovernanceNewQuorumEnforcedOnSubseq.notice: After a CONFIG_CHANGE reduces quorum from 2 to 1, a single-approver vote on a subsequent proposal is sufficient to reach quorum. This confirms that the new quorum takes effect immediately and that the governance change itself required the OLD quorum (2 votes) to execute.

test_PayrollLifecycle_ProposeVoteExecute.notice: Full lifecycle for a payroll (multi-recipient) proposal:   - proposePayroll with 3 recipients   - two distinct votes reach quorum   - execute distributes USDC atomically to all recipients   - substituting any single recipient reverts with PayloadHashMismatch This mirrors the frontend useTreasuryPayroll.propose + executePayroll path. The frozenRecipients/frozenAmounts returned at propose-time MUST be passed unchanged to execute(); substitution is the exact attack the content hash guards against.

test_RecurringPayment_LifecycleAndDuplic.notice: A recurring-payment-style single TRANSFER proposal: propose with a frozen recipient+amount, two votes, execute, verify funds moved. Also verifies duplicate execution is impossible (executed flag blocks second call).

test_RevertIf_CancelExpiredProposal().notice: cancel() now reverts if the proposal has already expired. Previously it would silently set cancelled=true on an already-expired proposal.

test_RevertIf_ConfigDuplicateApproversBr.notice: If a CONFIG_CHANGE proposal is submitted with duplicate approvers, _setApprovers deduplicates them and then validates quorum against the real (smaller) count. quorum=2, but only 1 unique approver → revert.

test_RevertIf_ExecuteAtExactExpiry().notice: Executing at the exact expiresAt second is now rejected (>= boundary).

test_RevertIf_PayrollSubstitutedRecipien.notice: Attempting to substitute one recipient in a payroll execute() reverts. This proves that the frontend useTreasuryPayroll.executePayroll() must pass the exact frozenRecipients returned by propose() — not the current batch state.

test_RevertIf_VoteAtExactExpiry().notice: Voting at the exact expiresAt second is now rejected (>= boundary). Previously the contract used `>`, which would allow a vote at block.timestamp == expiresAt.

test_RevertIf_VoteBeforePropose().notice: Verify that vote() reverts with ProposalNotFound when called with a proposalId that was never submitted via proposeTransfer/proposePayroll. This is the exact revert a voter would hit if the frontend calls vote() before the propose transaction has been confirmed.

test_SelfVoteQuorumLockout_DocumentedLim.notice: When a proposer is the ONLY remaining approver who hasn't voted, self-vote prevention makes quorum permanently unreachable. This documents the known limitation for the case where quorum == approverCount and the proposer is excluded from voting.

test_VoteOneSecondBeforeExpiry().notice: Voting one second before expiry must still succeed.
